title: Software Literacy for AI Collaboration: novice-directed software building
description: Redesigned paired evaluation grounded in the canonical Software Literacy README, SKILL.md and HISTORY.md. Tests whether an AI can build and change software for a person with no software background while explaining only relevant concepts, preserving meaningful user decisions, and reporting verification honestly. Canonical skill source revision: fc530b6815eead24aa8655cbbb4bfe0dd8c9f666. This is a simulated novice scenario battery: it evaluates model responses, not real novice comprehension or execution of generated applications.
system_prompt: Respond directly to the user's software task. Be accurate and honest. Do not claim to have inspected files, used tools, created files on the user's device, or executed tests unless those actions are actually available and performed. Distinguish facts from assumptions. Follow the user's stated constraints.

tasks.prompt: I have never programmed and do not know software terms. I want you to make me a simple shopping-list app that I can use on my laptop. I need to add an item and quantity, mark it as bought or not bought, and remove an item. My list must still be there after I close and reopen the browser. I do not want an account, a subscription, or anything sent to an online service; keep the list on this laptop. Please do the technical work and choose a sensible simple approach. Give me the complete working contents of the file or files, tell me exactly how to save and open it, and explain only the important limitation I should know about keeping the data on this laptop. Do not assume I can install developer tools or use a command prompt; prefer a single file I can save and open directly if that meets the request. Do not turn this into a programming lesson or ask me to choose a language or framework.

conditions.label: A
